reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Definitions for sections 196.010 to 196.120
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (13) and history note (L. 1943 p. 559 § 9857). Defines thirteen food, drug, device, cosmetic, labeling, new-drug, compendium, and person terms for sections 196.010 to 196.120.

headings.title: Factors in determining whether labeling is misleading
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs consideration of affirmative representations as well as omissions of material facts regarding labeling representations or customary/prescribed use consequences.

headings.title: Antiseptic labeling as germicide and prolonged-contact exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Treats antiseptic drug labeling as a germicide representation, except for drugs represented for inhibitory prolonged-contact uses such as wet dressings, ointments, or dusting powders.

headings.title: Scope of selling food, drugs, devices, or cosmetics
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Construes selling provisions in sections 196.010 to 196.120 to include manufacturing, processing, packing, offering, holding, dispensing, giving, and supplying in establishments.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.010:10124 (subsections 1–4, subdivisions (1)–(13), and L. 1943 history note) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked section-range scope (196.010 to 196.120), the device-definition carve-outs in subd. (3), soap exclusion in subd. (2), prolonged-contact antiseptic exception in subsec. 3, and the archived establishment wording in subsec. 4 (which omits "device" in its closing list). Retained all 4 drafted titles as accurate and neutral.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties for section 196.015 violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1943 p. 559 § 9860). Prescribes misdemeanor conviction for section 196.015 violations, punishable by up to $1,000 fine, one year imprisonment, or both. Review revision: changed to "penalties" to reflect alternative fine, imprisonment, or both.

headings.title: Guaranty exemption for section 196.015(1) or 196.015(3)
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Exempts a person from subsection 1 penalties for section 196.015(1) or 196.015(3) violations upon establishing a signed supplier guaranty under state or federal adulteration/misbranding law. Review revision: standardized singular section cross-reference and exemption phrasing.

headings.title: Advertising medium liability exception and disclosure condition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Exempts publishers, radio licensees, and ad media (excluding manufacturers, packers, distributors, or sellers) from false-advertisement liability unless refusing a DHSS request for the originator's name and address.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.025:10127 (subsections 1–3 and L. 1943 history note) and verified all fingerprints. Checked misdemeanor penalty range (fine, imprisonment, or both) for section 196.015 violations, the supplier guaranty exemption limited to section 196.015(1) or 196.015(3) (with federal 1938 act alternative), and the advertising-medium liability exception conditioned on DHSS disclosure requests. Revised titles 1 and 2 for penalty accuracy and singular section reference; retained title 3.

headings.title: Tagging and embargoing suspected adulterated or misbranded articles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective note (L. 1943 p. 559 § 9861, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634; Effective 1-2-79). Directs DHSS agents with finding or probable cause to tag and embargo suspected adulterated or dangerously/fraudulently misbranded articles and forbids unauthorized removal or disposal.

headings.title: Condemnation petition or removal of embargo tag
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires agents finding an embargoed article adulterated or misbranded to petition a circuit or associate circuit judge for condemnation, or remove the tag if compliant.

headings.title: Destruction, supervised sale, or bonded correction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Directs court-ordered destruction or supervised sale (net proceeds to general revenue) of condemned articles, with a bonded claimant option for paid DHSS-supervised relabeling or processing. Review revision: broadened to "bonded correction" to cover both proper labeling and processing.

headings.title: Perishable food condemnation, three-day hold, and summary hearing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Provides immediate condemnation/destruction of unsound or unsafe perishables with possessor agreement, or a three-day hold notice, immediate circuit court summary hearing, custody orders, and subsection 3 disposal. Review revision: tied "summary" strictly to the court hearing so consent-based immediate destruction is not mischaracterized.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.030:10128 (subsections 1–4, L. 1943/1978 history, and 1-2-79 effective date note) and verified all fingerprints. Checked probable-cause embargo authority and unauthorized-removal ban, circuit/associate circuit condemnation petition vs. tag removal, court-ordered destruction/sale or bonded relabeling/processing, and perishable condemnation (requiring possessor agreement for immediate action or a 3-day hold with immediate circuit court summary hearing). Revised titles 3 and 4 to capture relabeling alongside processing and tie "summary" strictly to the hearing; retained titles 1 and 2.

headings.title: Department rulemaking authority and federal-act conformity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1943 p. 559 § 9875, A.L. 1993 S.B. 52, A.L. 1995 S.B. 3). Vests enforcement rulemaking for sections 196.010 to 196.120 in DHSS and requires conformity with federal-act regulations insofar as practicable.

headings.title: Department and designee authority to conduct hearings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Directs that hearings authorized or required under sections 196.010 to 196.120 be conducted by DHSS or its designated officer, agent, or employee.

headings.title: Chapter 536 and section 536.024 rulemaking procedures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Requires regulations to follow chapter 536 and conditions chapter 196 rule effectiveness on promulgation under section 536.024.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.045:10131 (subsections 1–3 and L. 1943/1993/1995 history note) and verified all fingerprints. Checked DHSS rulemaking scope for sections 196.010 to 196.120 with federal-act conformity "insofar as practicable", department/designee hearing authority, and chapter 536 plus chapter-wide section 536.024 rule-effectiveness requirements. Retained all 3 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Nonprofit food preparation for charitable fund-raising events
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2014 S.B. 525). Permits ('may prepare') a nonprofit organization to prepare food in a private home or other area for distribution to end consumers at a charitable fund-raising event. Review revision: broadened beyond private homes to cover "a private home or other area".

headings.title: Optional consumer placard disclosing uninspected kitchen
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Permits ('may inform') posting a clearly visible serving-location placard stating the food was prepared in a kitchen not subject to regulatory inspection.

headings.title: Optional pre-event regulatory notice and contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Permits ('may notify') written or email pre-event notification to the regulatory authority, specifying required details if such notification is made. Review revision: reflected both optional notice and required details if sent.

headings.title: Exclusion of department-regulated food establishments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Excludes food establishments regulated by DHSS providing food for a charitable event from section 196.056. Review revision: replaced unexplained acronym with "department-regulated".

headings.title: Excluded charter counties, first-class counties, and cities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Exempts specified population-bracketed charter counties, any independent city, a multi-county home-rule city over 400,000, and specified first-class counties from section 196.056. Review revision: tightened to the excluded county and city classes.

headings.title: Preserved food-borne disease and outbreak investigation authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Clarifies that section 196.056 does not prohibit DHSS or local health departments from investigating food-borne disease or outbreaks. Review revision: included both food-borne disease and outbreak investigations.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.056:10134 (subsections 1–6 and L. 2014 S.B. 525 history note) and verified all fingerprints. Checked permissive ("may") framing of home/other-area nonprofit food preparation, optional consumer placard, optional pre-event notice with mandatory details if made, exclusion of department-regulated establishments, population-bracketed county/city exclusions, and preserved food-borne disease/outbreak investigation authority. Revised titles 1, 3, 4, 5, and 6 for fuller scope and clearer terminology; retained title 2.

headings.title: Publication of summaries of court judgments and orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1943 p. 559 § 9877). Permits ('may') DHSS to publish periodic reports summarizing judgments, decrees, and court orders under sections 196.010 to 196.120.

headings.title: Public health information dissemination and investigation reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Permits DHSS to disseminate information on foods, drugs, devices, and cosmetics for public health and fraud protection, and preserves authority to report and illustrate investigation results.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.065:10136 (subsections 1–2 and L. 1943 history note) and verified all fingerprints. Checked permissive ("may") authority to publish periodic judgment/decree/order summaries under sections 196.010 to 196.120 and to disseminate public-health and anti-fraud information while preserving investigation reporting and illustration authority. Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Criteria deeming food adulterated
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (12) and history note (L. 1943 p. 559 § 9865, A.L. 1994 S.B. 474, A.L. 2018 H.B. 2034). Enumerates twelve food-adulteration grounds covering poisonous/unsafe substances (referencing section 196.085), filth, diseased animals, containers, omitted/substituted constituents, confectionery alcohol/additives, and uncertified coal-tar colors.

headings.title: Industrial hemp not sole adulteration ground
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Provides that a food is not deemed adulterated solely because it contains industrial hemp or an industrial hemp commodity or product. Review revision: highlighted "not sole" qualifier directly in heading.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.070:35429 (subsections 1–2, subdivisions (1)–(12), and L. 1943/1994/2018 history note) and verified all fingerprints. Checked all twelve food-adulteration grounds—including the non-added substance qualifier in (1), section 196.085 cross-reference in (2), confectionery alcohol (<5%) and chewing-gum provisos in (11), and federal coal-tar batch certification in (12)—and the "solely" qualifier for industrial hemp in subsec. 2. Revised title 2 to surface the "not sole" qualification; retained title 1.

headings.title: Temporary permits for local microbial contamination risks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1943 p. 559 § 9867). Directs DHSS, solely upon investigation finding uncheckable post-commerce microbial contamination risk, to issue temporary permit regulations barring unpermitted introduction into commerce. Review revision: removed unstated "emergency" term, added local scope, and reflected potential contamination risk.

headings.title: Immediate permit suspension, hearing, and reinstatement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Authorizes immediate permit suspension upon notice for condition violations, with permit-holder right to apply for reinstatement following prompt hearing, inspection, and compliance finding.

headings.title: Inspection access and permit suspension for denial
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Grants designated DHSS personnel access to permitted establishments to verify compliance and makes denial of access grounds for suspension until access is freely given.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.080:10139 (subsections 1–3 and L. 1943 history note) and verified all fingerprints. Checked the narrow investigation-and-locality trigger for temporary microbial-contamination permits, immediate suspension on notice with prompt hearing/inspection reinstatement procedure, and inspection-access rights with suspension for denial. Revised title 1 to remove unstated "emergency" language and reflect local contamination risk; retained titles 2 and 3.

headings.title: Compliance with federal labeling requirements and misbranding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1943 p. 559 § 9870 through A.L. 2019 S.B. 514). Requires drug and device manufacturers, packers, distributors, and sellers to follow current Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act labeling rules, deeming noncompliant items misbranded.

headings.title: Prescription drug labeling exemption and mail-diagnosis exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Exempts drugs dispensed on electronic or signed written prescriptions of licensed physicians, dentists, or veterinarians bearing required dispenser/prescription label details, excluding mail-diagnosis dispensing businesses.

headings.title: Regulations exempting bulk off-site processing, labeling, or repacking
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Directs DHSS to adopt labeling/packaging exemptions for drugs and devices transported in trade for off-site bulk processing, labeling, or repacking, conditioned on compliance upon removal.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.100:47917 (subsections 1–3 and L. 1943/2001/2019 history note) and verified all fingerprints. Checked incorporation of current FFDCA labeling rules and misbranding consequence, the electronic/signed-written prescription exemption with required label elements and mail-diagnosis business exclusion, and DHSS rulemaking directive for bulk off-site processing/labeling/repacking exemptions conditioned on compliance upon removal. Retained all 3 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Annual tobacco manufacturer certifications, brand lists, and records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (5), continuation paragraphs, and history/effective note (L. 2010 S.B. 884; Effective 7-07-10). Requires April 30 certifications under penalty of perjury for participating and nonparticipating manufacturers, thirty-day supplemental brand-family notices, escrow/agent details, attribution disclaimers, and five-year record retention.

headings.title: Tobacco directory, listing exclusions, and agent emails
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and notes. Directs monthly first-day directory publication beginning January 1, 2011, bars noncompliant or escrow/judgment-delinquent nonparticipating manufacturers, and requires stamping agents to supply updated email addresses for notices. Review revision: removed "Monthly" to avoid implying mandatory monthly updates when text requires updates "when necessary" on the first calendar day of each month.

headings.title: Staggered directory effective dates and unlawful cigarette acts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and notes. Sets immediate manufacturer effectiveness, next-month first-day wholesaler effectiveness, and fifteenth-day retailer effectiveness, and prohibits purchasing, stamping, selling, holding for sale, or importing unlisted cigarettes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.1023:10302 (subsections 1–3, all subdivisions and continuation paragraphs, L. 2010 history, and 7-07-10 effective note) and verified all fingerprints. Checked April 30 perjury certifications, 30-day supplemental brand-family updates, nonparticipating escrow/agent disclosures (noting archived internal cross-reference "as required in this subsection" in subsec. 1(3)(a)), state attribution disclaimer, 5-year recordkeeping, Jan 1, 2011 directory updated when necessary on the first calendar day of each month, exclusions, stamping-agent emails, and staggered effective dates/prohibitions. Revised title 2 to avoid implying mandatory monthly updates; retained titles 1 and 3.

headings.title: Service-of-process agent for unregistered nonparticipating manufacturers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective note (L. 2010 S.B. 884; Effective 7-07-10). Requires unregistered nonresident or foreign nonparticipating manufacturers to continually maintain a Missouri service-of-process agent with proof to the director as a condition precedent to directory listing. Review revision: specified unregistered nonparticipating manufacturers and avoided adding "resident" absent from subsection 1.

headings.title: Notice and proof for terminating or replacing agents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires thirty-day advance notice before terminating an agent and replacement proof five days before termination, or five-day notice with replacement proof if an agent terminates. Review revision: clarified notice and replacement-proof duties for both manufacturer- and agent-initiated terminations.

headings.title: Deemed service on secretary of state without directory qualification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Deems noncompliant nonparticipating manufacturers selling cigarettes in Missouri to have appointed the secretary of state for service of process, while clarifying that deemed appointment does not satisfy directory listing prerequisites.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.1026:10303 (subsections 1–3, L. 2010 history, and 7-07-10 effective note) and verified all fingerprints. Checked condition-precedent Missouri service-of-process agent requirement for unregistered nonresident/foreign nonparticipating manufacturers, 30-day/5-day termination and replacement notice/proof deadlines, and deemed secretary-of-state service without satisfying directory prerequisites. Revised titles 1 and 2 for exact party scope and termination/replacement clarity; retained title 3.

headings.title: Quarterly stamping agent reports and five-year record retention
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) and (2), continuation paragraph, and history/effective note (L. 2010 S.B. 884; Effective 7-07-10). Requires stamping agents within twenty days after each quarter to report cigarette and roll-your-own stick counts by brand family and retain supporting nonparticipating-manufacturer invoices for five years.

headings.title: Information sharing between director and attorney general
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Directs the director to disclose requested compliance information to the attorney general and requires mutual sharing of sections 196.1003, 196.1020 to 196.1035, and corresponding sister-state law information.

headings.title: Director authority to require financial-institution escrow proof
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Authorizes ('may, at any time, require') the director to obtain proof from a nonparticipating manufacturer's escrow financial institution showing principal balance, deposits, and withdrawals.

headings.title: Additional compliance information and packaging or labeling samples
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Permits the director to require stamping agents or manufacturers to submit additional compliance information, including packaging or labeling samples for each brand family.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.1029:10304 (subsections 1–4, subdivisions (1)–(2), continuation paragraph, L. 2010 history, and 7-07-10 effective note) and verified all fingerprints. Checked 20-day quarterly (or more frequent) stamping-agent reports for cigarettes and roll-your-own stick counts plus 5-year nonparticipating-manufacturer invoice retention, director/AG disclosure and sister-state sharing, discretionary financial-institution escrow proof, and additional compliance info/sample requests. Retained all 4 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: License revocation or suspension and civil penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective note (L. 2010 S.B. 884; Effective 7-07-10). Permits revoking or suspending stamping-agent licenses under section 149.035(3) and imposing civil penalties up to the greater of 500% of retail value or $5,000 per section 196.1023(3) violation.

headings.title: Contraband seizure, forfeiture, and destruction of unlawful cigarettes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Declares cigarettes judicially found sold, offered, or possessed in violation of section 196.1023(3) contraband subject to chapter 149 seizure, forfeiture, and destruction without resale.

headings.title: Attorney general injunctions and recovery of state litigation costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Authorizes attorney general injunctions against actual or threatened section 196.1023(3) or section 196.1029(1)/(4) violations by stamping agents, with potential recovery of investigation costs and attorney fees.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor for prohibited cigarette distribution or import
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Criminalizes as a class A misdemeanor selling, distributing, holding, transporting, or importing cigarettes known or reasonably known to be intended for distribution violating section 196.1023(3). Review revision: removed "knowing"-only wording because text applies where a person "knows or should know" of intended unlawful distribution or sale; covers acquire/hold/own/possess/transport/sell/distribute/import.

headings.title: Deemed unfair practice under section 407.020
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Deems any violation of section 196.1023(3) an unfair practice violating section 407.020. Review revision: matched statutory "unfair practice" wording.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.1032:10305 (subsections 1–5, L. 2010 history, and 7-07-10 effective note) and verified all fingerprints. Checked permissive stamping-agent license revocation/suspension (section 149.035(3)) and civil penalties (up to greater of 500% retail value or $5,000 per violation), judicial contraband forfeiture/destruction under chapter 149, AG injunctions against stamping agents with discretionary state cost/fee recovery, class A misdemeanor under the "knows or should know" standard, and deemed unfair practice under section 407.020. Revised titles 4 and 5 for mens rea and statutory wording accuracy; retained titles 1, 2, and 3.

headings.title: Judicial review of directory listing or removal decisions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2010 S.B. 884, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1298 Revision). Subjects a director's decision not to list or to remove a brand family or manufacturer to review by a court of competent jurisdiction.

headings.title: Perjury-certified compliance prerequisite for chapter 149 licenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Prohibits issuing or renewing a chapter 149 license without written certification under penalty of perjury of full compliance with sections 196.1020 to 196.1035.

headings.title: Director rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability clause
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Authorizes director rulemaking under chapter 536 and section 536.028 and voids rulemaking authority and post-August 28, 2010 rules if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

headings.title: Tobacco Control Special Fund custody, investment, and reversion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Creates the Tobacco Control Special Fund with state treasurer custody under sections 30.170 and 30.180, appropriation-limited administrative use, investment credit, and biennial reversion of remaining moneys to general revenue.

headings.title: Disgorgement of violation profits and cumulative remedies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Directs courts finding sections 196.1020 to 196.1035 violations to order disgorgement of profits, gains, or receipts to the Tobacco Control Special Fund and declares remedies cumulative.

headings.title: Precedence of section 196.1003 and model-statute safeguard
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Makes section 196.1003 control in irreconcilable conflicts and invalidates any portion of sections 196.1020 to 196.1035 that would disqualify section 196.1003 as an MSA qualifying or model statute. Review revision: replaced "severability" with "model-statute safeguard" to reflect partial-invalidity wording.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.1035:10306 (subsections 1–6 and L. 2010/2014 history note) and verified all fingerprints. Checked judicial review of directory denials/removals, perjury-certified compliance prerequisite for chapter 149 licenses, chapter 536/section 536.028 rulemaking with post-Aug 28, 2010 nonseverability clause, Tobacco Control Special Fund custody/investment/biennial reversion (noting duplicate "hereby created" phrasing across subsecs. 4 and 5), mandatory disgorgement and cumulative remedies, and section 196.1003 precedence/MSA-disqualification invalidity. Revised title 6 to replace "severability" with "model-statute safeguard"; retained titles 1–5.

headings.title: Federal or state application requirement for new drugs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note (L. 1943 p. 559 § 9871). Prohibits selling, delivering, holding, or giving away a new drug absent an effective 21 U.S.C.A. § 355 application or, if not federally subject, safety testing and a complete state application to DHSS. Review revision: removed "selling"-only wording to cover delivering, offering, holding, and giving away.

headings.title: Sixty-day effective date and refusal of state applications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Makes state applications under subsection 1(2) effective sixty days after filing unless DHSS, after notice and hearing opportunity, issues a prior refusal order finding the drug unsafe. Review revision: specified "state applications" matching subdivision (2) of subsection 1.

headings.title: Exemptions for investigational, preexisting, and federally licensed drugs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and notes. Exempts labeled expert-investigational drugs, pre-enactment state or interstate drugs, and drugs licensed under the 1902 Virus, Serum, and Toxin Act (retaining archived 'U.S.C. 1934 cd.' citation text). Review revision: replaced unstated "biological" label with "federally licensed" referencing the 1902 Virus, Serum, and Toxin Act.

headings.title: Revocation of orders refusing new-drug applications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Authorizes ('may be revoked') DHSS to revoke an order refusing to permit a new-drug application to become effective.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.105:10144 (subsections 1–4, subdivisions, and L. 1943 history note) and verified all fingerprints. Checked 21 U.S.C.A. § 355 or state safety-testing/application prerequisites covering selling/delivering/offering/holding/giving away new drugs, 60-day effective date and hearing-based refusal orders for state applications, exemptions (investigational, preexisting, and 1902 Virus, Serum, and Toxin Act licensed drugs retaining archived "U.S.C. 1934 cd." typo), and permissive revocation of refusal orders. Revised titles 1, 2, and 3 for scope precision; retained title 4.

headings.title: Exclusive opioid treatment and prevention uses for settlement proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2020 H.B. 1682 through A.L. 2023 H.B. 402/S.B. 45 & 90/S.B. 106). Restricts attorney general opioid settlement proceeds solely to opioid addiction treatment, prevention, and related health care and law enforcement costs.

headings.title: Opioid Addiction Treatment and Recovery Fund administration and nonreversion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and notes. Creates the dedicated nonreverting fund in state treasurer custody under sections 30.170 and 30.180 for use by DMH, DHSS, DSS, DPS, DOC, and the judiciary, with investment earnings credited to the fund. Review revision: covered fund administration, investment earnings, and nonreversion across subdivisions (1) through (3).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.1050:54165 (subsections 1–2, subdivisions (1)–(3), and L. 2020/2022/2023 history note) and verified all fingerprints. Checked exclusive opioid treatment/prevention and related health-care/law-enforcement restrictions on AG opioid settlement proceeds and establishment of the dedicated, nonreverting Opioid Addiction Treatment and Recovery Fund (custody under sections 30.170 and 30.180, six named state agencies/judiciary, section 33.080 nonreversion, and investment earnings). Revised title 2 to cover administration and nonreversion across all subdivisions; retained title 1.

headings.title: Life Sciences Research Trust Fund deposits and nonreversion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2003 H.B. 688). Establishes the separate trust fund receiving twenty-five percent of MSA moneys starting FY 2007, restricts appropriations outside sections 196.1100 to 196.1130 absent majority vote of each house, and bars section 33.080 reversion.

headings.title: Strategic life sciences research and commercialization purposes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Directs strategic cooperative use of trust fund moneys with governmental and nonprofit entities to build Missouri life sciences research capacity, attract institutions, and commercialize technologies.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.1100:10307 (subsections 1–2 and L. 2003 H.B. 688 history note) and verified all fingerprints. headings.title: Reserve or peer-reviewed capacity-building awards of undistributed funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2003 H.B. 688, A.L. 2011 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 7, A.L. 2026 S.B. 890). Directs holding undistributed section 196.1112 DED appropriations in reserve or awarding them via peer review for nonprofit/public research capacity initiatives; note official heading still says 'Board's powers' while 2026 text assigns powers to DED.

headings.title: Permissive department grant, peer-review, facility, and funding powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (6) and notes. Subject to section 196.1130 limits, permits DED to issue grants/contracts, establish peer review panels, contract support services, acquire/lease facilities, employ staff, and administer moneys.

headings.title: Two-percent administrative expense cap and appropriation exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Directs maximizing funds for research capacity and caps DED's administrative spending at two percent of appropriated, reserve, and other moneys unless the general assembly appropriates limited additional administrative funds.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 196.1115:60462 (subsections 1–3, subdivisions (1)–(6), and L. 2003/2011/2026 history note) and verified all fingerprints. Verified archived discrepancy where official heading retains "Board's powers" while 2026 S.B. 890 body text vests authority in the department of economic development. Checked undistributed section 196.1112 reserve/peer-reviewed award mandate, permissive DED powers subject to section 196.1130, and 2% administrative expense cap with legislative-appropriation exception. Retained all 3 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Four-part cost reimbursement test and department guidelines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (4), continuation paragraph, and history note (L. 2003 H.B. 688, A.L. 2026 S.B. 890). Requires cost reimbursement under a four-part reasonableness/connection/consistency/conformance test and permits DED rules, guidelines, and permitted-cost explanations.

headings.title: Research freedom, recipient intellectual property ownership, and rules
